AJ Mohammad Ali with Kayser Kamal, Advocates ----- For the Petitioners. 
MA Sobhan with Shadia Afrin, Advocates ----- For Respondent No. 2.
parties:
Gulshana Ara Begum and others ------ Petitioners
VS
Judge Artha Rin Adalat No. 1 Dhaka and another ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Zinat Ara J: In this Rule Nisi, the petitioners have called in question the legality of Order No. 9 dated 15-9-2015 passed by the learned Judge of Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka (respondent No. 1) in Artha Jari Case No. 46 of 2015 (Annexure-E to the writ petition), rejecting an application filed by the petitioners under section 27(2) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 read with Order XXI, rule 30 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 to transfer the said Artha Jari Case in proper court for execution. 

 2. M/s Sheema Apparel, a proprietorship concern of Irin Alam, in course of its business, obtained loan (letters of credit loan) from respondent No. 2, Sonali Bank Limited, Local Office, Sonali Bank Bhaban, Motijheel, Dhaka (shortly stated as the Bank). As a security to the loan, Irin Alam, Gulshana Ara Begum, Imtiaz Alam Riya and Ivy Alam Sumi mortgaged 285 Aujutangsha of land situated at Paikpara, Narayanganj in favour of the Bank by mortgage deed No. 7790 dated 18-10-2009. The aforesaid persons also executed personal guarantees and other charge documents i.e. demand promissory note, DP Note, delivery letters, etc. in favour of the Bank. M/s Sheema Apparel and others opened back to back letters of credit (L/C) and imported yarns, fabrics, etc., but failed to export the goods and to repay the loan of the Bank. Whereupon, the Bank created forced loan against the said L/Cs, as the Bank had to pay the L/C amounts. Thereafter, the Bank repeatedly requested the principal borrower and third-party mortgagors and guarantors to repay the loan, but of no avail. In the aforesaid circumstances, the Bank, as plaintiff, filed Artha Rin Suit No*. 227 of 2013 before Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka (briefly stated as the Adalat) impleading M/s Sheema Apparel, Irin Alam and the petitioners as defendants of the suit for recovery of loan amounting to Taka 2,45,69,205 as stood on 31-5-2013 along with interest till realization thereof. The defendant-petitioners filed a written statement in the suit denying the allegations brought against them. Eventually, the defendant-petitioners and other defendants did not contest the suit. As a result, the suit was decreed ex parte by judgment and decree dated 10-7-2014. The judgment-debtors having failed to pay the decretal dues, the Bank, on 7-4-2015, filed Artha Jari Case No. 46 of 2015 before the Adalat. In the execution case, the judgment-debtor-petitioners, on 1-9-2015, filed an application under section 27(2) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (hereinafter stated as the Ain) read with Order XXI, rule 30 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (shortly stated as the Code) to transfer Artha Jari Case No. 46 of 2015 in a proper court for execution of the decree. The learned Judge of the Adalat rejected the said application by the impugned order. 

 Petitioners' Case 

 3. The loan was obtained by M/s Sheema Apparel from the Bank and as a security to the loan, a property situated at Narayanganj was mortgaged by the judgment-debtors to the Bank, which is beyond the territorial jurisdiction of the Adalat and therefore, the continuation of the execution case in the Adalat situated in Dhaka for selling the mortgaged property situated at Narayanganj is not lawful. In such situation, the petitioners filed the application for transfer of the Artha Jari Case to an Adalat having proper territorial jurisdiction and so, it ought to have been allowed by the Adalat. But it was rejected by the learned Judge of the Adalat by the impugned order unlawfully. 

 Respondent No. 2's Case 

 4. Respondent No. 2-the Bank has contested the Rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition denying the material averments made in the writ petition and supporting the impugned order. It has been stated that under section 27(1) of the Ain, the learned Judges of Artha Rin Adalats have full jurisdiction to execute a decree relating to Artha Rin Suits; that the property having been mortgaged with the Bank situated in Dhaka relating to the loan, the learned Judge of the Adalat has full jurisdiction to execute the decree passed by it; that the provision of section 27(2) of the Ain has no manner of application in the instant case inasmuch as here there is separate Artha Rin Adalat in Dhaka and also at Narayanganj; that the writ petition is misconceived, a delaying device and the Rule is, thus, liable to be discharged. 

 5. Mr AJ Mohammad Ali, the learned Advocate for the petitioners appearing with Mr Kayser Kamal, takes us through the writ petition, the application filed by the petitioners before the Adalat for transfer of the execution case, other connected materials on record and submits that under Order XXI, rule 30 of the Code read with section 27(2) of the Ain, an execution case that requires for selling or disposal of the immovable property, situated outside the territorial jurisdiction of a court passing the decree has to be transferred to the court having territorial jurisdiction in which the property is situated. He next submits that the scheduled immovable mortgaged property is situated at Narayanganj and therefore, the Artha Rin Adalat situated in Dhaka district had no jurisdiction to take initiative regarding execution of the decree so far as it relates to auction sale of the mortgaged property. He further submits that if auction sale of the mortgaged property is held at Narayanganj, where the mortgaged property is situated, with adequate local publicity, in such case, the property would be sold at maximum available price and therefore, the interest of the judgment-debtors would be protected. He finally submits that in the facts and circumstances, the impugned order rejecting the application filed by the Bank is unlawful and liable to be struck down. 

 6. In reply, Mr MA Sobhan, the learned Advocate for the Bank appearing with Ms. Shadia Afrin, takes us through the affidavit-in-opposition, the connected materials on record, the impugned order, the relevant provisions of Order XXI, rule 30 of the Code and section 27 of the Ain and contends that Order XXI, rule 30 of the Code has no nexus relating to transfer of execution cases. He next contends that from sub-section (1) of section 27 of the Ain, it is evident that the decree has to be executed by the Adalat by which the decree has been passed. He also contends that the provision of sub-section (2) of section 27 of the Ain is not applicable in the instant case inasmuch as the provision of sub-section (2) of section 27 of the Ain is completely relating to different circumstances. He further contends that in the facts and circumstances of the case, the learned Judge of the Adalat lawfully passed the impugned order to proceed with the execution case, as the property was mortgaged with the Bank situated in Dhaka district and the mortgaged property has to be sold by the Adalat, which is executing the decree of the Artha Rin Suit. He finally contends that in the facts and circumstances of the case, the impugned order is legal and the Rule is misconceived and thus, liable to be discharged with costs. 

 9. Admitted facts of the case have already been narrated hereinbefore. Therefore, it needs no further discussions. 

 10. At the outset, it be mentioned that Order XXI, rule 30 of the Code is not relating to transfer of execution cases from one court to another. So, this provision has no manner of application in the instant case. 

 “২৭(২) এই আইনের অধিনে দুই বা-ততোধিক জেলার জন্য একটি মাত্র অর্থঝণ আদীলত প্রতিষ্ঠিত হইয়া থাকিলে এবং উক্ত অর্থখণ আদালত কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত রায় বা আদেশ হইতৈ আবশ্যই হয়, যাহা অর্থঝণ আদালত যে জেলায় অবস্থিত, উক্ত জেলা হইতে ভিন্ন, তাহা হইলে আদালত, যে জেলার অর্থঋণ আদালত অবস্থিত, সেই জেলা জজের মাধ্যমে জারী মামলাটি কার্যকর করিবার জন্য উপরিল্লিখিত ভিন্ন জেলার জেলা জজের নিকট প্রেরণ করিবে। The Schedule & property of this execution case is not so far from this court. Under the above circumstances, as an executing Court the petition brought by the judgment debtor is not tenable in this case. 

 13. Thus, it is evident that under section 27(1) of the Ain, Artha Rin Adalat may execute a decree passed by it or the said Adalat may also transfer the execution case for execution to another Artha Rin Adalat and in such case, the latter Adalat would execute the decree. 

 14. Section 27(2) of the Ain as quoted hereinbefore provides a situation where there is only one Artha Rin Adalat for two or more districts and in such situation, if the property is situated at different districts, then the execution case is to be sent to the District Judge for execution of the decree through a court, which would be treated as Artha Rin Adalat. 

 15. In the instant case, the Artha Rin Adalat is not for two or more districts. Rather, admittedly, in Dhaka district, there are several Artha Rin Adalats. Thus, the provision of section 27(2) of the Ain cannot be said to be applicable in the instant case. 

 17. Mr Ali also agrees that the Artha Rin Adalat which passed the decree may also execute a decree in appropriate cases. 

 18. Be that as it may, admittedly, in the instant case, the mortgaged property is situated at Narayanganj district and the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that if the execution case is transferred to Artha Rin Adalat, Narayanganj through District Judge and local publicity is made by publishing auction notice, beating drums, etc., then the mortgaged property would be sold at a higher price. He also submits that if the mortgaged property is sold in Dhaka, there is every likelihood that it will not be sold at appropriate price and for the interest of the judgment-debtors as well as the Bank for recovery of the decretal dues, the mortgaged property ought to be sold at Narayanganj. 

 19. We have already seen that under section 27(1) of the Ain, the Artha Rin Adalat is empowered to transfer an execution case to a different district and the mortgaged property having been situated at Narayanganj, we are of the view that the execution case has been lawfully filed before the Adalat, but the execution case ought to have been transferred to Artha Rin Adalat, Naraynaganj for execution of the decree relating to the mortgaged property situated at Narayanganj so that the property is sold at the maximum price. If the mortgaged property is sold at a maximum price, both the Bank and the judgment-debtors would be benefited by it. Therefore, the learned Judge of the Adalat ought to have allowed the application for transfer of the execution case to a Court of Narayanganj district. 

 20. Thus, considering the overall circumstances, we are of the view that the learned Judge of the Adalat was not justified in not transferring the execution case for selling the mortgaged property by the Artha Rin Adalat, Narayanganj through the District Judge. 

 26. The impugned order No. 9 dated 15-9-2015 passed by the learned Judge of Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka (respondent No. 1) in Artha Jari Case No. 46 of 2015 (Annexure-E to the writ petition) is, hereby, declared to be not justified and thus, set-aside. 

 27. The learned Judge, Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka is directed to pass necessary order for transfer of Artha Jari Case No, 46 of 2015 to Artha Rin Adalat, Narayanganj through the District Judge for execution of the decree relating to the mortgaged property.
